title: Last census: 0.79 to 0.88 million counted, sources differ
why: No census since; every later figure is an estimate. Sources give 785,543, 793,396, 861,399 or 875,250.

title: UNRWA dataset shows 103,137 registered Palestine refugees in Lebanon
why: Earliest value in the UNRWA series; reaches 197,974 by 1975 and 306,471 by 1990.

title: Tourist arrivals peak near 1.4 million before civil war
why: One source says 2.4 million pre-war visitors; definitions differ. Only 180,000 by war's end. Page: 1974 benchmark of roughly 1.4 million tourists.

title: Population growth halves in first full war year
why: UN series: +33,278 in 1976 against +58,006 in 1975 (2.69 million at war start).

title: Israeli invasion pushes over 120,000 to Beirut suburbs
why: Early case of war displacement toward Beirut's southern belt, a pattern repeated in 2006, 2024 and 2026.

title: Largest civil-war displacement wave: about 367,000 in Mount Lebanon
why: Mountain-area displacement still shaped return politics after Taif.

title: Ministry for the Displaced created after Taif
why: Institution set up to fund returns; only about 20% of displaced went back by 1999.

title: War ends: airport handled 637,944 passengers that year
why: Post-war baseline for the airport series; 1 million crossed in 1992. Airport table: 637,944 in 1990.

title: 1991-1999: about $800 million spent, about 20% of displaced returned
why: Only 9% got full house-reconstruction reimbursement; 450,000 still displaced in 1995 (14%).

title: Airport passes one million passengers (1,092,645)
why: First million-passenger year after the war. Airport table: 1,092,645 in 1992.

title: Emigration 1992-2018: 602,227 net departures, about 22,305 a year
why: General Security departures minus arrivals; 1998 was a net-arrival year (+8,323). Some scholars say real outflow is higher.

title: UNDP-type estimate: about 810,000 (28%) forced from homes in the war
why: Conflicts with 'up to one million' peak (FMR). Search summary, not opened.

title: Tourist arrivals hit post-war low of 424,000
why: World Bank series low; arrivals then grow to 2.17 million by 2010.

title: Rare net-arrival year: 8,323 more Lebanese arrived than left
why: Only year in the 1992-2018 General Security series with net return.

title: Airport runways hit and airport closed in 34-day war
why: Airport article dates closure 13 July; the war article says runways were destroyed 12 July.

title: Airport reopens to commercial flights with MEA and Royal Jordanian
why: Reopened before the 14 Aug ceasefire was a month old; blockade lifted 7-8 Sep (sources differ by a day).

title: Airport traffic falls 37% to 2.46 million
why: From 3.89 million in 2005; recovers to 4.0 million by 2008.

title: Tourist arrivals record: 2.168 million
why: Series peak (World Bank); airport 5.5 million the same year.

title: UNHCR registers 126,939 Syrians by year-end, up from 124 in 2011
why: Start of the exponential phase; 851,284 a year later.

title: Population jumps 508,000 in one year to 5.74 million
why: UN/World Bank total counts Syrians; UNHCR registered 851,284 by year-end.

title: UNHCR-registered Syrians peak at 1,147,494 at year-end
why: Government says 1.5 million in all; registration halted May 2015, so UNHCR counts fall afterwards.
dup_of: UNHCR registers over one million Syrian refugees

title: Population peaks at 6.47 million, then falls to 5.70 million by 2020
why: Fall of 770,000 combines emigration, Syrian departures and model revisions.

title: Airport record: 8.84 million passengers
why: All-time high; 2019 was 8.69 million. Airport table: 8,841,966 in 2018.

title: Emigrants 18,863 in 2018, per Information International
why: From General Security data; 2018-2021 total 195,433 (2017-2021: 215,653). Search summary only.

title: Protesters block roads to the airport
why: Travellers reported walking out of the terminal; airport itself stayed open. Search summary.

title: Airport closed for COVID until 1 July
why: Reopened at about 10% of capacity; 2020 traffic 2.49 million, down 71%. Closure start date approximate.

title: Port blast damages airport terminal moderately; flights continue
why: Airport stayed the country's lifeline while the port was destroyed.

title: 79,134 emigrants in 2021 versus 17,721 in 2020
why: Better sourcing than the existing entry; LAU SOAS gives 77,777. 53% were doctors, engineers and other skilled workers.

title: Airport back to 6.35 million passengers
why: Airport table 6,349,967 (another summary: 6,352,446); 2019 was 8.69 million. Airport table: 6,349,967 in 2022.

title: UNRWA starts digital identity verification in Lebanon
why: Mid-2023 to mid-2025 exercise to count who actually lives in Lebanon; per a UNRWA staff post in search results.

title: Airport reaches 7.13 million passengers
why: Best year since 2019 before the 2024 war; another summary gives 7,102,847 passengers. Airport table: 7,127,649 in 2023.

title: About 500,000 displaced within days of the 23 Sept strikes
why: Foreign Minister figure via Wikipedia; 111,000 had been displaced from Oct 2023 to 22 Sep 2024 (OCHA).

title: UN: over one million displaced, 100,000 flee to Syria, more than in 2006
why: OCHA: 90% fled in the last week. UNRWA opened 9 shelters for 3,350 people.
dup_of: Over one million displaced by late September 2024

title: Airport falls 21% to 5.62 million passengers
why: War year cut the airport heartbeat; airport stayed open.

title: UNHCR-registered Syrians fall 29.5% to 532,357
why: Drop of 223,069 in one year after Assad's fall; UNHCR counts 379,000-400,000 returns, authorities 500,000+.

title: Airport recovers to 7.01 million; tourist arrivals 1,635,490 (+44.59%)
why: Airport still 19% below the 2018 record. Airport table: 7,011,129 in 2025; the 1,635,490 (+44.59%) tourist figure appears on Tourism in Lebanon page under a different year label, so year not confirmed.

title: IOM: 2.85 million departures, 2.63 million arrivals, net outflow 220,279
why: Covers all border crossings; World Bank/UN model says -10,230. Sources disagree by a factor of 20.

title: UNRWA: 487,869 registered but only 231,515 verified as resident
why: Digital ID check halves the headline Palestinian figure; 2017 census counted 174,422 in camps and gatherings. Search summary.

title: UNHCR data: 64,417 still displaced a year after ceasefire
why: Matches the IOM figure in the existing entry; UNHCR stock 123,774 at end-2024.

title: About 273,000 Syrians remain registered with UNHCR
why: Down from 755,426 at end-2024; Wikipedia Syrians in Lebanon, read. Page: 273,094 registered in Jan 2026; end-2024 figure not confirmed (page has 774,697 for Jun 2024).

title: Airport stays open while airlines suspend flights; MEA carries on
why: Reports say foreign carriers left for about 40 days and MEA flew reduced schedules. Search summaries, not opened.

title: Displacement peaks above 1.2 million (IOM)
why: Peak higher than the 1 million in existing entries; 330,000 still displaced by Sept and 810,000+ returned or moved nearby.
dup_of: War resumes 2 March; over one million displaced

title: Airport January-April traffic 1,242,700, down 32.84% year on year
why: BLOMINVEST report of 9 July 2026; arrivals 566,296, departures 676,382.

title: IOM: 646,107 displaced begin returning; about 500,000 remain
why: Figures from data collected since 22 June, after a ceasefire on 21 June; many southern villages inaccessible.
dup_of: IOM: 646,107 displaced begin returning; about 500,000 remain

title: Airport January-August 2026: 3,581,861 passengers, down 24.17%
why: August alone 835,903, down 10.04% on August 2025: partial recovery.
